data.title: Russia to ban P2P crypto trading from July 2027 – Here’s why
data.description:
Russians have just eight months to trade Bitcoin [BTC], Ethereum [ETH], and other crypto assets with each other. 

Starting from the 1st of July, 2027, this direct crypto trading among peers that does not need a regulated third party, also known as peer-to-peer (P2P) trading, will become illegal. 

This is part of Article 30 of the Federal Law No. 282-FZ (On Digital Currencies and Digital Rights). The legislation was signed into law in August by President Vladimir Putin and became effective on the 1st of September 2026. 

In fact, the same framework allowed a new licensing regime for firms and banks that want to operate crypto exchanges and act as digital asset custodians. Already, Russia’s largest bank, Sberbank, has got two licenses and plans to offer crypto trading from December. 

While the new Russian crypto regulation regime could accelerate institutional adoption, the strict rules against P2P and self-custody transfers may squeeze out some retail investors. 

Why is Russia banning P2P and self-custody crypto transfers

Per the new rules, crypto trading will only be permitted via “entities organizing the circulation of digital currencies” or regulated platforms. That rules out P2P transfers. 

Additionally, withdrawals to self-custody are banned. Russian users can send assets from self-custody wallets to regulated entities. But they can’t move the funds to self-custody wallets. Unlike P2P transfers, which will be outlawed by 2027, the self-custody withdrawal ban is already effective. 

Foreign stablecoins such as Tether’s USDT are permitted for public trading on regulated platforms. Put simply, the Russian government will have full visibility into crypto capital flows, including custodied assets. 

Interestingly, killing P2P and self-custody withdrawals removes crypto blind spots that most global regulators are trying to address. 

For Russia, the tight rules also include a cap for retail crypto investments at $3.5K per year. Crypto will not be used for payments locally in Russia, but it will be allowed for cross-border and international trade. 

In other words, Russia wants to rein in capital flight by limiting citizens from moving funds to offshore and self-custody platforms.

This will also ensure better transparency and reduce tax evasion. At the same time, importers and exporters will be allowed to use crypto for international trade, likely to bypass sanctions. 

Global P2P crypto transfers surge 300% to $230B

Globally, Brazil, Thailand, the EU zone, and other jurisdictions are adopting nearly similar tight P2P and self-custody transfers. But they seek to deal with anti-money laundering, fraud, and tax evasion, making their policy incentives slightly different from Russia’s. 

That said, global P2P and personal wallet flows increased +300% to $228B in the past year, according to Chainalysis. This underscores rising user distrust in the traditional system and regulated entities. But governments want to crack down hard on this loophole. 

Final Summary

  • Russia to ban P2P crypto transfers by July 2027. 
  • Global P2P flows increased 3x to $230 billion in 2026 amid a heavy government crackdown.

data.title: Quantus CEO leads 9-firm alliance to standardize crypto’s quantum defenses
data.description:
Quantus, Midnight, and seven other blockchain firms have formed a Quantum Alliance to fast-track post-quantum readiness across the industry. 

According to Christopher Smith, Founder and CEO of Quantus, the plan is to standardize post-quantum products that can easily be adopted across the crypto industry.

He added,

Our intention with the Quantum Alliance is to front-load a lot of the complex decision-making when making post-quantum blockchain products and create standards that others can simply pull off the shelf as the industry migrates.

The work will span migration, zero-knowledge (ZK) proofs, wallet security, and chain interoperability. On each track, the team wants to harmonize rules that can ensure smooth operations as blockchains adopt different post-quantum signatures.

There have been intensified calls for accelerated preparations for the post-quantum era following recent fears that advanced AI may just offer similar threats to quantum computing. 

So far, the Quantum Alliance and the BlackRock-backed Bitcoin Security Consortium are the only two groups that have gone public to push for a post-quantum blockchain industry. Earlier this week, Coinbase heightened calls for accelerated phased migration for Bitcoin to avoid falling behind the security push. 

So, what’s really at stake? 

$2.7T at risk as firms push for post-quantum migration

According to Migration Fail, nearly $2.7T of the crypto market is at risk of a quantum threat. In fact, based on a quantum readiness assessment, Bitcoin has a ‘D’ while Solana and Ethereum have an ‘F’ rating. 

Only Quantus and 3 other chains have an A rating because they have already leveraged post-quantum (PQ) signatures. Starknet, which has made considerable progress in its PQ push, has a B rating. 

Tron has already announced that it is ready to deploy its network PQ upgrade on the mainnet anytime in Q4 2026. 

The rest of the blockchains have issued PQ plans. Some are in the testing phase, while others have no concrete plans at all. Still, some experts believe a working quantum computer could be feasible as early as 2028. Hence, the aggressive push to have most blockchains quantum-ready by 2029. 

Whether the deadline will be met remains uncertain. Already, the industry, led by Ethereum founder Vitalik Buterin, is undecided on which post-quantum schemes are safe for long-term applications. 

The recent updates show the industry acknowledges the urgency of the quantum threats. However, whether the industry will migrate before 2029 remains unclear. 

Final Summary

  • Quantum Alliance has been formed to assess the industry’s post-quantum readiness and accelerate migration 
  • The update comes days after Coinbase urged the industry to begin phased migration.

data.title: Crypto traders embrace AI for research – But can they trust it to trade?
data.description:
The cryptocurrency market remains extremely volatile, with capital movements trending in ways that require traders to find an edge in the market. The crypto market has reversed sharply over the last ten days following a bullish run from mid-September to early October.

Since the 5th of October, the total crypto market capitalization (excluding stablecoins) recorded an outflow of roughly $233.49 billion, despite rallies in between, suggesting growing selling pressure.

One approach traders are exploring is the use of artificial intelligence (AI). Reports indicate that traders remain skeptical about using AI for trade execution but rely on it for research to improve their trading outcomes.

Crypto traders rely on AI mainly for research

According to a recent MEXC report based on a survey conducted between the 14th and 20th of September, which covered over 3,800 respondents, crypto traders are increasingly relying on AI.

According to the survey report, about 68.9% of respondents confirmed that they use AI in their trading. However, traders mostly use AI before executing trades.

News summaries accounted for the largest share, with 54% of respondents noting that they rely heavily on AI for this purpose. Other notable use cases included analyzing the market, finding opportunities, and explaining concepts, which accounted for 48.6%, 38.0%, and 34.5% of respondents, respectively.

Only a few respondents use AI after trading, representing 8.5% of the group. Before trading, most traders rely on general-purpose AI tools, including ChatGPT and Claude. However, traders also said they prefer in-exchange AI and chat features, with 62.7% indicating this preference.

In an email to AMBCrypto, Vugar Usi Zade, CEO of MEXC, noted that the growing interest in AI has yet to translate into widespread readiness for fully automated trading.

“We see growing user interest in AI, but it is too early to speak of widespread readiness for full autonomy. Even among those who have experimented with automated execution, one in two fears that they might not notice a problem in time to stop it.”

Agent tokens fall despite rising trading volume

Although traders widely use AI agents for crypto trading, investors have yet to show increased interest in AI agent-related tokens.

Market activity shows significant weakness in prices, which have declined roughly 7% in the past day, with market capitalization now valued at $2.368 billion.

At the same time, the volume for these tokens has surged 28.4% to reach $524 million. When prices decline and volume rises, it suggests further weakness in the market.

The performance could be due to a lack of trust in AI agents more broadly, with the report showing a similar trend. Only 13% of respondents, or 482 people, had tried using AI agents in the market. Around 50.1% of respondents expressed interest in AI agents but had not tried using one.

Risk in the market remains a critical concern, with traders who responded to the report confirming that incorrect trades, account security, and technical barriers or complexity have deterred investors from allocating funds.

Most investors expressed interest in using automation; they said they would allocate no more than 20% of their account funds to it, even with risk limits in place.

Final Summary

data.title: Taiwan blocks Kalshi and Coinbase websites over suspected election betting
data.description:
Taiwan has blocked access to the websites of prediction-market platform Kalshi and crypto exchange Coinbase over suspected election betting. Bloomberg reported the restrictions on October 15, citing a court ruling it reviewed.

The action comes ahead of November’s local elections and adds to the legal challenges facing prediction markets. In Taiwan, betting on election results can carry criminal penalties, including when wagers take place online.

Court order restricts website access

A New Taipei court authorized Taiwan’s communications regulator and internet registry to restrict domestic access to both platforms.

The Criminal Investigation Bureau said it requested the order over suspected violations of the Public Officials Election and Recall Act. Some Coinbase users reported losing access to the website on October 14.

The bureau’s reasons for seeking to impose restrictions included maintaining the integrity of elections and preventing foreign attempts to meddle in them. However, they provided no evidence suggesting that both Kalshi and Coinbase ever handled funds from China.

​The current development does not mean that either company broke the law.

Taiwan’s election-betting rules extend online

Article 103-1 directly refers to placing bets over the internet and other means of electronic communication with regard to election/recall results.

The offence carries up to six-months imprisonment on summary conviction for those placing the bets. Those who do so as organizers for profit could be exposed to five years in prison. The sentences above are the maximum length of penalty under the law, not those received in the above case.

In April, the Taiwanese Taoyuan District Prosecutors Office announced that it had begun an investigation based on information that the public had been using cryptocurrency to bet on the outcome of Taiwanese local elections on Polymarket. 

That separate case shows election-betting enforcement predates the latest restrictions.

Kalshi also faces U.S. regulatory challenges

Kalshi is also facing US regulatory challenges, for which the dispute between prediction market participants partly focuses on who should regulate them within the US. 

As AMBCrypto previously reported, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission is arguing that the activities of these prediction platforms fall under its authority, which challenges state efforts to treat sports contracts as gambling.

New York is arguing differently. Its attorney general sued Kalshi in July, alleging that it operated an unlicensed gambling business.

Final Summary

Taiwan has reportedly blocked Kalshi and Coinbase websites over suspected election betting ahead of local polls.

The restrictions come as U.S. authorities argue about how prediction markets should be regulated.

data.title: USDC faces stricter EU oversight – What changes for Circle under MiCA?
data.description:
The European Banking Authority (EBA) recently named USD coin [USDC] as the first major e-money token in the European Union under MiCA.

According to the EBA, the decision has introduced tighter regulations on Circle’s stablecoin. This includes the introduction of new supervisory rules from the 12th of November 2026. Thereafter, EBA will be monitoring Circle’s capital, reserves, liquidity, and redemption guarantees.

On the other hand, Circle’s governance and operational activities will still fall within France’s ACPR.

The EBA stated that Circle must meet several key elements. This includes holding at least 60% of USDC reserves in segregated bank accounts.

Previously, non-significant issuers had to keep only 30% or more of their stablecoin reserves in segregated bank accounts. These additional requirements have significantly increased Circle’s compliance obligations.

Additionally, the close relationship that the EBA has developed with New York State Regulators supports the regulation of Circle’s operations.

Ultimately, the designation could reinforce USDC’s role in regulated European payments. This is if Circle meets the stricter requirements without disrupting liquidity or redemption access.

Circle CCTP expands beyond USDC

The Circle’s regulatory reach is mirrored by Circle’s efforts to increase the uses for which it can provide service via its cross-blockchain network. Its Cross Chain Transfer Protocol (CCTP) has now moved over $100 million in non-USDC assets using CirBTC, EURC, and WETH.

This represents Circle’s ability to take the same transfer system used on one blockchain network and expand it to other networks as well.

This expansion of the number of supported assets was initiated by EURC being added in September and then adding CirBTC in late September, which accelerated the process.

 

Continued growth in terms of sustained monthly increases in use and acceptance of the CCTP across destination blockchains.

Euro stablecoins struggle for market share

Despite numerous attempts to increase the utilization of Euro-Pegged Stablecoins, they remain a relatively small percentage of the digital asset market.

Notably, their share reached just 0.25% of combined euro and dollar stablecoin supply by October 2026, fluctuating between 0.15% and 0.27% since January 2024.

This limited growth highlights the challenge of attracting demand beyond established dollar-based markets. Currently, Euro stablecoins stand at $768 million. This shadows the $306.5 billion figure for dollar-pegged tokens.

Source: Blockworks

However, Qivalis, a consortium of 37 European banks, was granted an e-money license to issue a Euro stablecoin. Their distribution networks could help attract users and businesses.

The ultimate test for Euro Stablecoins will come down to user and business adoption across various platforms, including on-chain trading, lending, and payments.

Final Summary

  • USD Coin faces stricter EU oversight due to Circle’s expanding regulated stablecoin footprint.
  • USDC expands its utility as a cross-chain system, while Euro Stablecoins face challenges competing against dollar dominance.

data.title: ‘Not that important to us’ — Saylor downplays MSCI’s plan to drop Strategy
data.description:
MSCI will proceed with its plan to delete Strategy, Metaplanet, and other crypto treasuries from its Global Investable Market Indexes. 

The firm announced the move after finishing its month-long consultation process on the proposal to exclude “non-operating companies.” 

During the consultation window, Bitcoin treasury firms, including Strategy and Strive, opposed the proposal. Even TD Cowen backed the two firms, arguing that their digital credit operations using Bitcoin holdings as collateral make them “operating firms.”

The final list of firms to be delisted will be made available on 11th November 2026, as part of the November index review. 

MSCI will discontinue, effective with the November 2026 index review, the interim measures announced on October 10, 2025 in respect of the preliminary list of companies whose digital asset holdings represented 50% or more of total assets.

According to the MSCI, Strategy and Metaplanet will be axed from its indices after the November review.

A couple of other crypto treasuries, including Sharplink, DeFi Dev Corp, Ton Strategy, Canton Strategic Holdings, Capital B, Sui Group Holdings, Upexi, and Solana Company, will be on the watchlist for now. 

In other words, they could be next in line for deletion if they fit the non-operating company profile and trigger the new exclusion criteria. 

Potential impact on Bitcoin and crypto treasuries sector?

The proposal was first floated last year. However, it was paused after massive outcry that it only targeted the crypto sector. The new 2026 proposal was slightly expanded beyond just crypto treasuries, but key players in the sector will still be the most affected. 

According to JPMorgan analysts, the deletion could trigger $2.8B in forced selling pressure and outflows from MSCI indices. If other indices such as FTSE Russell and S&P Dow Jones follow suit, the outflows could increase to $8B-$11B. 

The forced MSTR sales, expected towards the end of November, could derail Strategy’s financing model for its Bitcoin acquisition and the so-called digital credit plans. 

For his part, Michael Saylor, Founder of Strategy, downplayed the impact of the development. 

Not that important to us…They’re imposing prejudicial values on digital assets. Digital assets are smarter, faster, and stronger. MSCI may not want to share in it, but investors and the nation will disagree.

Analyst Simon Dixon disagreed with Saylor though, despite contending that MSTR will still survive. 

That’s a lot of passive buying pressure taken off the table. $BTC wrapped in FIC financial products and digital credit is not resistance to banks. It is subordinate to banks and their financial engineering games.

Crypto treasuries hold over $100B worth of assets across Bitcoin, Ethereum, HYPE, SOL, and more. With a key demand line pulled off the table, it’s now unclear how the sector will readjust or hold up. 

Final Summary

  • Metaplanet and Strategy could be axed from MSCI global equity benchmarks by November.
  • Over $100B worth of crypto holdings held by public companies could be on the line.

data.title: Midnight price prediction – Can NIGHT defend KEY support and rally 26%?
data.description:
Midnight [NIGHT] has shed 12% this week as of writing, amid inflation-driven broader market weakness. But the pullback has hit a crucial short-term support level at $0.041 that could give bulls a new entry opportunity if the macro landscape improves.

Will Midnight crypto defend its price range?

Since late September, NIGHT’s price has been range-bound, swinging between $0.052 and $0.041. If the sideways action extends ahead of the Fed rate decision at the end of October, then the range highs and lows could still offer trading opportunities. 

That would mean a 26% upside potential could be feasible if the range low of $0.041 is defended. 

But the sideways outlook would be invalidated if price falls below the moving averages shown above. That would flip the market structure bearish. In such a scenario, a greater downside risk to $0.035 or $0.029 could not be ruled out. 

Such a deeper risk-off move could be confirmed if the RSI slips below the neutral level and price dips below the moving averages. 

Liquidation data suggests a potential NIGHT price reversal

On the 1-month liquidation heatmap, the largest liquidity pool was concentrated right above the $0.05 level. This upside liquidity pool denoted leveraged short sellers that could trigger a short squeeze and a potential price reversal. 

In other words, in a likely volatile market situation, the upside target of $0.053 could be tagged. If so, NIGHT’s 26% upside potential could become feasible. 

However, if U.S. inflation worsens and drags Bitcoin [BTC] lower, then NIGHT may break below its short-term support and price range. 

Midnight promises institutional privacy and has been riding on the broader privacy narrative that lifted Zcash and other assets. However, the privacy segment has trended lower and consolidated in the past few weeks. 

Given that NIGHT is also moving in lockstep with the privacy segment, its next move may be determined by the sub-sector. 

Overall, NIGHT’s retested a typical short-term price range low that could attract buying demand if the broader privacy market recovers. But in case of another risk-off move, the sideways structure could be broken. 

Final Summary

  • Midnight price correction has hit a short-term support and range low at $0.041
  • A strong rebound at the support could offer a 26% potential gain if the broader market does not experience another risk-off move.

data.title: LayerZero surges 23% – Why ZRO’s price rally faces THESE risks
data.description:
After losing $2 support and falling to a low of $1.8, LayerZero [ZRO] made a strong comeback amid a broader market trend reversal.

The altcoin successfully defended the $2 level and climbed to a local high of $2.25 at press time, after gaining 23% on the daily charts. 

Is LayerZero’s demand returning?

The market largely recovered, driven by renewed interest in the derivatives. Previously, ZRO, like most altcoins, saw a collapse in derivatives, which intensified downside pressure. 

Now, it seems the trend has reversed.  As a result, the altcoin’s Open Interest (OI) surged 31% to $275 million, while the derivatives volume rose 63% to $336 million as of writing. 

The rising OI alongside volume implied increased market participation and steady capital flow into new positions. Meanwhile, the altcoin’s Long/Short Ratio rose above 1 across all tracked exchanges.

At these levels, the ratio implied that traders were overly bullish and largely opened new and expanded existing long positions. 

Two major hurdles remain for ZRO

Despite the recent gains, LayerZero faces both short and long-term risks. For short-term concerns, the altcoin is experiencing heavy profit-taking. 

After the trend reversed the past day, inflows into exchanges skyrocketed, with over $26 million entering exchanges. As a result, the Spot Netflow rose above $3.5 million. 

An elevated positive Netflow implied that deposits outpaced withdrawals over the said period, a clear sign of aggressive profit realization. 

Typically, when profit takers dominate the market, it raises selling pressure, which usually precedes market weakness. 

Additionally, community chatters have raised concerns about the upcoming unlocks. On the 20th of October, LayerZero will unlock 25.7 million ZRO, worth approximately $56.5 million at the current price. 

Proxonchain reported that previously, these unlocks have resulted in an over-double-digit slip. This raises concerns about the trend’s long-term sustainability, and given prior behavior, the market could drop. 

What do momentum indicators suggest?

Structurally, even with the recent price hike, the momentum is yet to confirm an upside. At the time of writing, the MACD sat below its signal line, suggesting that downward pressure remains strong.

Likewise, the Relative Vigor Index (RVGI) confirmed this trend of weakness, remaining in the negative zone and continuing to decline. 

These two indicators suggest that bearish pressure is relatively strong and that bullish pressure is insufficient to prompt a trend reversal. 

Therefore, if the profit taking persists, we could see LayerZero fail to extend the rally and fall below $2. The upcoming unlocks will make things worse and intensify the downside, with $1.8 as critical support. 

For now, if the recent speculative demand holds, ZRO could clear the $2.4 resistance and target $2.5.

Final summary

  • LayerZero surged 24%, defended $2, and rose to a local high of $2.25 amid renewed demand.
  • ZRO’s rally attracted increased profit-taking, raising concerns about another pullback alongside upcoming unlocks.

data.title: Injective crypto surges 25% – Can INJ confirm a breakout above $9.60?
data.description:
Injective [INJ] has rallied 25% in 24 hours, is up 30% in a week, and is up just over 70% over the past month. AI and big data tokens have seen a strong performance in the past 24 hours, CoinMarketData showed, with the entire sector up 8.87% in a day.

The Injective crypto revenue/fully diluted value ratio was 20% above Arbitrum [ARB] and also led Solana [SOL], the Layer 1 blockchain, as shown in a post on X.

It was over 8x higher than Ethereum [ETH], too. Revenue/FDV is “one of the clearest measures of whether a network’s valuation is backed by real usage,” the post read.

This on-chain revenue flows into the INJ community buyback program, removing INJ supply each month and aiding token scarcity.

News of the Gulf Labs partnership helped boost Injective crypto token prices, and bullish derivatives trading data solidified the short-term sentiment as bullish.

Injective crypto challenges long-term bearish order block

Technically a bearish breaker block, the $6.93-$9.17 area was an area of supply that stretched back to November. It briefly served as a demand zone during the October sell-off, but Injective crypto prices fell to new lows early in 2026.

At the time of writing, this breaker block on the weekly timeframe was being tested. Additionally, the swing move down from $16.55 to $2.65 has its 50% level at $9.6. The other retracement levels overhead at $11.24 and $13.57 are the next swing resistances to watch.

Is Injective crypto on track for a bullish breakout?

A weekly session close above $9.60 would be a good sign of a bullish continuation. In the lower timeframes, such as the H4 above, the breakout past $8.50 was also a sign of bullish intent.

Notably, the OBV continued its uptrend that began in early September, and the trading volume in recent sessions was well above the 20-period Moving Average. Additionally, at press time, the RSI was at 72, indicating strong bullish momentum.

Swing traders can wait for a pullback toward $8.50 to buy. Long-term investors will want to see prices climb past $13.575 comfortably before looking for signs of a long-term trend shift.

Final Summary

  • Injective crypto has rallied 25% in a day on the back of strong spot and derivatives demand for the altcoin.
  • The high revenue/FDV ratio and the Gulf Labs partnership exploring tokenization have helped set up the bullish breakout.

data.title: OCC flags 9 top U.S banks for debanking crypto industry between 2020-2025: Report
data.description:
According to an OCC report, the nine largest U.S banks, including JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America (BoA), and Citibank, denied or limited banking access to crypto firms and founders.

The Office of the Comptroller of Currency (OCC) said it reviewed 100,000 debanking complaints across top banks between 2020 and 2025. 

The report added,

Banks had policies that required, encouraged, or otherwise influenced banks to deny or limit access to financial services to Americans because of their political or religious beliefs or affiliations or their lawful business activities.

Ideally, such debanking or restricted access is allowed if there is objective financial risk. However, the 9 banks conducted their restrictions based on political affiliations and reputational considerations, instead of financial risks. 

Crypto is just one of the six industries that were affected by the debanking spree. Speaking on the same, Comptroller Jonathan Gould claimed that they will root out the practice. 

We are working to end politicized debanking. Access to banking should be based on financial risk, not political beliefs or whether a lawful industry is out of favor.

OCC, FDIC seek an end to crypto debanking

The debanking was rampant during the Biden era, and most crypto firms and founders decried the targeted restriction. 

Although the allegations, also known as Operation Chokepoint 2(OCP), were widely covered across crypto media, they went mainstream after a16z’s Marc Andreessen discussed them publicly.

At the time, the U.S Congress opened a probe into it. Last August, President Donald Trump issued an executive order to banking regulators to investigate the claims. 

The OCC investigation has been going on for over a year now, with the released 47-page report confirming that debanking was not merely an allegation. 

Nic Carter, Founder of VC firm Castle Island Ventures, echoed the same and noted, 

Bombshell report from the OCC out today confirming what we all suspected. We weren’t imagining it. OCP2.0 was real.

For his part, Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan called the debanking policy “disgraceful and dangerous.”

It’s worth noting, however, that banking regulators have tried to ensure that another debanking spree never happens. 

In August, for instance, the OCC and FDIC finalized a rule to define “unsafe practices” and close a loophole that banks leveraged to arbitrarily enforce debanking. According to the regulators, the move would return banks to “risk-based supervision” in an effort to unwind Operation ChokePoint 2.0.

Banks fight back against crypto

So far, crypto firms have gained entry into banking systems. Some, such as Ripple and Circle, have been granted trust bank charter licenses to expand their stablecoin and crypto custody operations. 

However, banks and Senate Democrats are pushing against the trend, warning of financial stability risks. In fact, one of the banking groups sued the OCC over the trust bank charter approvals. 

With Democrats expected to regain control of Congress after the November midterms, it’s unclear whether the aggressive policy against crypto will return as well.

Final Summary

  • OCC found that debanking practice was widespread among top 9 U.S banks across 6 industries, including crypto.
  • Despite regulators’ push to avoid the unlawful restrictions, banks are still pushing against crypto firms.
